d: The most common functional ovarian cyst. A follicle fails to rupture and keeps filling with fluid, forming a thin-walled simple cyst that usually resolves within one to three cycles.
Cancer that has spread to both ovaries, made of mucin-filled signet-ring cells and usually coming from a stomach primary. The ovaries are enlarged and solid.
An ovarian epithelial tumor with atypia and stratified cells but no destructive invasion of the stroma. Its peritoneal implants are usually noninvasive, and surgery cures most patients.
A TP53-mutant carcinoma confined to the lining of the fimbriated end of the fallopian tube. It is the precursor of most high-grade serous carcinomas and is often found in BRCA carriers.
Glomerulus-like structures, each with a central blood vessel wrapped by tumor cells. They are the microscopic hallmark of the AFP-secreting yolk sac tumor.
Small follicle-like rosettes of granulosa cells around pink material. Together with grooved coffee-bean nuclei, they identify the estrogen-making granulosa cell tumor.
The Ovarian-Adnexal Reporting and Data System, an ultrasound scoring system that sorts an adnexal mass into risk categories, from almost certainly benign to high risk of malignancy.
The raised, bright plug in the wall of a mature cystic teratoma where hair, teeth and other tissues gather. It casts a shadow on ultrasound and is also called the dermoid plug.
